features.headline: Whether it's against backup QBs or not, the Bills' defense is rolling
features.desc: Buffalo will face another backup QB in Week 11 with Kyle McCord set to start in place of Malik Willis for the Dolphins.
body: ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The Buffalo Bills are executing something about as close to a midseason worst-to-first transformation as you'll ever see, albeit with a massive caveat.

Less than one month ago, the Bills trudged through their bye week with the NFL's 30th-ranked scoring defense and 31st-ranked total defense. So naturally in the weeks since, the Bills have allowed the fewest points and second fewest yards among the teams that have played three games.
It's been a steep turnaround for a Bills defense that's gone from the unit holding back the highest-scoring offense to a strength in its own right.

But that turnaround has also coincided with the Bills playing almost exclusively against backup quarterbacks, a trend that'll continue when the Bills (8-1) host the Miami Dolphins (1-8) at Highmark Stadium on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS).
So, as obvious as the answer might seem, it's worth asking the question: Is the game really that different when you're facing an NFL backup quarterback rather than a starter?

"It's definitely not the starters," Bills safety Amani Hooker told ESPN. "Nothing's easy. But it's just like anything else. The better talented guy is off the field in any position, it's not good for their team. I'm sure they feel the same way."

"I don't get to choose who I play. I just play," defensive lineman Ed Oliver adds. "Hell, who cares? If I got to choose who I could play, s—-. I guess it would be a starter. But you don't get to choose. That's kind of how football works. People get hurt. Next man up."

features.headline: Breaking down the Players Era 8 Houston-Kansas championship game
features.desc: It's a Big 12 showdown in Las Vegas. How did Houston and Kansas each get here, and how will they match up?
body: The Players Era 8 championship is here, and it's an all-Big 12 affair.
No. 8 Houston — which took down No. 1 Florida in the first semifinal game — will take on No. 11 Kansas — which eked by West Virginia in the second — tonight (11 p.m. ET on ESPN) in Las Vegas.

The Gators and Mountaineers will battle it out for third place (2:30 p.m. ET, ESPN), but all eyes are on the Cougars and Jayhawks, whose star player, Tyran Stokes, is questionable due to a bone bruise for the series finale.
ESPN college basketball writers Jeff Borzello and Myron Medcalf have been following every contest of this tournament. More below.
Two teams that know each other well plus two coaches who know each other well equals an early-season litmus test to determine the Big 12 favorite.

The availability of Kansas' Tyran Stokes will make a sizable difference heading into the game. If Stokes is able to play, he gives Bill Self another physical athlete who can make shots from the perimeter and is a menace in transition.
Stokes wouldn't back down from a war of attrition against Sampson's team.

For Houston, Dedan Thomas Jr. is the top name on the scouting report. He was fantastic against Florida — and Miles Sadler showed Wednesday night that Kansas can be susceptible to dynamic, aggressive guards.

The key for Houston defensively will be keeping Kansas out of transition and forcing the Jayhawks into a half-court game. With Trey Kaufman-Renn as a face-up 5, Kansas is capable of picking teams apart in the half court.
But it is far more effective when pushing the ball and scoring quickly — especially if Stokes suits up.

features.headline: Which of these 15 pass catchers should you trust going forward?
features.desc: A look at wide receivers and tight ends who have become start-worthy, and others you should expect less from.
body: With the fantasy football trade deadline looming (Dec. 2), I'll have a column next week on the top candidates to move. So, to build up to the deadline, this is a good opportunity to write about my current trust levels with pass catchers in the league.
These are wide receivers and tight ends who are trending up and those who are starting to lose my trust based on their usage, route deployment and declining production.

I'm not saying there are cut candidates in here, as most players still have some level of value, but the point of the column is to give managers the data and analysis they need to make lineup decisions in the critical weeks ahead.
There are 15 players below broken down into four separate categories: pass catchers to trust, not to trust, those to expect less from and also a couple of deeper-league targets.
Diggs can still shake coverage. It's on the tape. And he can catch touchdowns, too. Diggs, who has six scoring receptions on the season, now has a TD in three of his past four games.
Diggs is also scoring 14.4 fantasy PPG during this stretch, averaging seven targets per game.

While Diggs isn't an explosive playmaker at this stage of his career, he has the inside/outside alignment flexibility to gain positive matchups for quarterback Jayden Daniels, plus he is slippery after the catch.
With some positive matchups looming (CIN, @ARI, @TEN), I like Diggs as a WR2/flex.
Moore has been banged up this season, and he has missed time. However, in the five full games Moore has played, he has scored at least 12 fantasy points in four of them, with 16 or more in three.

features.headline: Historic usage rates are fueling Luka Doncic and the Lakers' offense
features.desc: Doncic is pushing the boundaries of basketball production. But could that actually hurt the Lakers' title hopes?
body: Is there such a thing as too much Luka magic?

That question might seem blasphemous to Los Angeles Lakers fans savoring Luka Doncic's scorching start for the NBA's third-ranked offense, but it's one worth monitoring as he pushes the boundaries of basketball production.
Doncic has jumped to the front of the NBA MVP conversation by averaging 38.1 points per game, which would eclipse Michael Jordan for the highest scoring average since the 1976 NBA/ABA merger.

But the Lakers guard is also posting a historic usage rate — the percentage of his team's possessions he ends with a shot attempt, free throw attempt or turnover — that sidles him with one of the heaviest offensive burdens in league history.
Given that ultra-high usage stars have always fallen short of winning a championship, should Doncic's heavy load start to raise alarm bells?
Los Angeles is tied for the league's best record at 13-3, largely because none of its opponents have effectively slowed down Doncic, who already has seven 40-point and two 50-point performances.
The Lakers have a juicy plus-15.3 net rating when the Slovenian star is on the court and have racked up seven double-digit victories.

L.A.'s extraordinary reliance on Doncic rekindles a debate about the perils of ball dominance. When one player is so responsible for his team's success, it leaves the roster exposed if he sustains an injury and increases the possibility the player might succumb to diminishing returns.
This is well-worn narrative territory that dates back decades: Jordan needs to pass more. Allen Iverson can't do it by himself. Russell Westbrook is a ball hog.

features.headline: Messi vs. Ronaldo, Man Utd hire Moyes: GTA V came out in a different soccer world
features.desc: As Grand Theft Auto VI is finally unleashed, here is what was happening in the world of soccer when the previous game was released 13 years ago
body: Given that it's the only thing anybody appears to be talking about, you may be aware that a new video game by the name of "Grand Theft Auto VI" was released on Thursday, thus ending a long and arduous 13-year wait among fans of the infamous Rockstar Games franchise for a new instalment.
The previous game in the series, GTA V, was launched what feels like an eon ago during the primordial mists of September 2013. Almost a decade-and-a-half later, GTA VI is finally upon us.
We couldn't help but ponder just how the soccer landscape has changed during those intervening years — or not, as the case may be.

- Mr. Worldwide: Meet soccer star who's played for clubs on 6 continents - MrBeast, meet Haaland: Man City star puts YouTuber through gauntlet - Why Champions League's iconic 'star' match ball may soon be replaced
One thing which is the same as it was in 2013 is Spain's dominance over men's international competition.

On the release of GTA V, La Roja were reigning world and European champions after winning the UEFA European Championship in 2008 and 2012, either side of their triumph at the 2010 FIFA World Cup, in an unprecedented era of back-to-back-to-back glory.
Skip forward 13 years and Spain — inspired by the likes of Lamine Yamal — are back on top having emerged triumphant at both Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup.
And now Spain's women's team is along for the ride, too, winning the Women's World Cup in 2023 and heading into next year's tournament as favorites.
Excelling on either side of the Clásico divide, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo were at the peak of their respective powers in 2013 at Barcelona and Real Madrid respectively.

features.headline: Skubal to ...? What about other big free agents? How MLB offseason dominoes fall
features.desc: Based on what ESPN's Jeff Passan is hearing, we predict where the top names available will land — and how they impact each other.
body: The countdown to the impending lockout is getting closer, which means the MLB offseason will likely grind to a depressing halt when the clock hits midnight on Dec. 1.

Until then, teams are continuing to act like it's business as usual — Jake Bauers to the Boston Red Sox, Dustin May to the Chicago White Sox and Evan Phillips to the Atlanta Braves have been the most significant free agent signings so far.
The big prize in a weak class is two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal — and he's expected to sign before the sport shuts down.

This happened prior to the last lockout following the 2021 season, when Corey Seager, Marcus Semien, Javier Baez, Max Scherzer, Robbie Ray and Kevin Gausman all signed $100 million-plus contracts before the lockout went into effect.
Skubal might be the only nine-figure free agent this year, but the ripple effect of where he lands will dictate the offseason.
Using Jeff Passan's intel on what he's hearing will happen over the next two weeks as a guideline, let's kick off this offseason edition of dominoes with Skubal going... East?
The Mets are the favorite to land Skubal, according to Passan, in part because of the Los Angeles Dodgers' desire for a shorter-term commitment.

Of course, Skubal loved his time with L.A. and lives in Arizona in the offseason, so maybe the Dodgers will view this as a situation of "sign him while you can" and eventually give Skubal whatever it takes.
If the labor negotiations do eventually end up with some sort of capped system, this could be the last chance for the Dodgers to empty their bank vault for several years.
